query: For an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy protective coating susceptible to progressive plastic deformation during continuous loading, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain its creep resistance? Specify the governing factor and rationale, an unspecified controlled comparison that would reveal it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, the operating boundaries under sustained stress, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, approximately 1 μm-thick FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings produced from Al0.2CrFeNi and Al targets.
generation.intervention: The modulation period (individual layer thickness, λ) was varied among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm by RF magnetron sputtering to create multilayers dominated respectively by coherent heterointerfaces (M8), semicoherent heterointerfaces (M16), or grain boundaries (M32 and M80), followed by nanoindentation creep testing.
generation.conditions: Deposition used a base pressure of about 5 × 10^-4 Pa, Ar flow of 100 sccm, working pressure of 0.3 Pa, 150 W on the HEA target, alternating 0/30 W on the Al target, and a 1 h deposition. Room-temperature nanoindentation used a 5 mN maximum load, loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s, a 100 s hold, and 20 s unloading; indentation depths were maintained at approximately 1/10–1/7 of the coating thickness.
generation.structural_mediator: Transformation from dual-phase lamellae to a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces.
generation.mechanism: Coherent interfaces enable preferential dislocation transfer from the softer FCC phase to the harder B2 phase, relieving stress concentration, while the hierarchical pattern activates multiple deformation mechanisms (dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, twins) to accommodate plasticity and ensure homogeneous strain distribution.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to multilayers dominated by coherent interfaces or grain boundaries, the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibits the greatest room-temperature creep resistance and a transition from dislocation-mediated creep to atomic-diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep.
generation.baseline: The comparison baseline comprises M8 (λ = 8 nm, coherent interfaces) and M32/M80 (λ = 32/80 nm, grain-boundary-dominated interfaces), which show predominantly dislocation-mediated creep.
generation.boundary: The result applies to the studied approximately 1 μm FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni sputtered multilayers under room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation creep at loading rates of 1–0.01 mN/s. Absolute creep displacement and steady-state-rate trends changed with loading rate, but the authors report the λ = 16 nm sample as having the strongest creep resistance based particularly on the stress-exponent trend. No elevated-temperature or macroscopic-creep boundary was established.

falsification_experiment.design: XRD and TEM/IFFT distinguished phase peaks and coherent versus semicoherent interfaces. Load–displacement and normalized displacement–dwell-time nanoindentation curves measured creep displacement and strain rate, while linear fits of ln(strain rate) versus ln(flow stress) yielded the creep stress exponent n used to distinguish diffusion/interface-slip creep (n around 1–2, with nanoindentation values potentially somewhat higher) from dislocation creep (n > 3).
measurements: XRD and TEM/IFFT distinguished phase peaks and coherent versus semicoherent interfaces. Load–displacement and normalized displacement–dwell-time nanoindentation curves measured creep displacement and strain rate, while linear fits of ln(strain rate) versus ln(flow stress) yielded the creep stress exponent n used to distinguish diffusion/interface-slip creep (n around 1–2, with nanoindentation values potentially somewhat higher) from dislocation creep (n > 3).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
